695d2bdf9c103cd607cdab89cffb8d32bd111f3c.summary: Research paper and project page describing 'Cloak & Dagger', Android attacks that abuse the draw-on-top and accessibility permissions to take control of the UI feedback loop. The authors say that when an app is installed from Google Play, these permissions may be granted without user notice, enabling clickjacking, keystroke recording, PIN stealing, device unlock, two-factor token theft and silent installation of a god-mode app. A 20-person user study found no user noticed. hedges: Most of these attacks are due to design issues, and they are thus challenging to prevent.
Some functionality may work 'as intended'; the report says this functionality can still be abused.
Google's partial fix applies only on Android 7.1.2 and only to normal permissions, per the report.
Whether automatic grant of draw-on-top is deliberate is stated only 'to the best of our understanding'.
Previous Android versions are said to be 'very likely' vulnerable; the report did not test them.
Some bugs were marked 'won't fix' and the report says they will not be fixed.
